metadata.title: Efficient Hierarchical Coding Agent Tree
metadata.purpose: Convert a human task into a verified artifact through a frozen acceptance contract, a layered verification ladder, and a task-class-based model routing policy — while keeping the architect's and PM's context lean.

primary-optimization-targets.metric: Active context tokens per agent per step

non-goals.item: Maximizing model intelligence at every node
Adding verification layers for redundancy without a named failure class

design-principles.principle: The architect's competence is not in reading worker code. It is in freezing the contract, owning the verification ladder, and reading a ledger of criterion → disposition → evidence digest. The architect must never need to read a subagent transcript to accept or reject work.

principle.name: Decidable checks belong in the harness, not the prompt

design-principles.principle: Classes that are decidable belong in a script, never in an agent prompt. Agents miss them because the prompt lists them among many checks and attention drifts; the script never drifts. Every prompt rule must either teach judgment or declare an invariant. If it can be scripted, script it.

Each convention lives in exactly one instruction layer; other layers point to it or stay silent. Duplicating a rule across layers creates a drift bomb: change one copy and you have authored a silent contradiction.

principle.name: Cheapest model that clears the threshold

design-principles.principle: Route each chunk to the least expensive model whose cost-per-passing-build and reliability@k clear the chunk's risk threshold. Escalate only on failure or on an unmet threshold. Pareto Crewing: heterogeneous crews match best fixed crew quality at up to 25× lower cost given a ≥80%-accurate verifier. Defect-repair case: uniformly low-cost crew statistically indistinguishable from frontier crew at one-fifteenth the cost.

principle.name: Hidden suite selects; self-reports never do

design-principles.principle: A build can pass its own tests yet still be wrong. Agent-generated tests frequently execute successfully but exhibit weak assertions and missing edge cases (the execution-adequacy gap). Selection is by the frozen hidden acceptance suite the worker cannot read or edit.

pass@k measures whether at least one attempt succeeds — useful for acquisition. pass^k measures whether all k attempts succeed — the metric for customer-facing reliability and delegation scope. Per-run reliability 0.90 → pass^8 = 0.43 (fails in ~4 of 10 eight-step sessions). τ-bench: frontier models above 60% average success drop below 25% at pass^8. CodeBench: mean hidden-test pass rate 0.80 vs strict resolve rate 0.20 (4× inflation in single-rollout proxies).

Freeing working context is achieved by loading only what the current step requires, not by writing shorter prompts. Progressive disclosure + a context firewall + harness enforcement together minimize active context.

principle.name: Cross-family verification for correlated blind spots

design-principles.principle: When the same model writes and reviews, the checker shares the maker's priors — same training distribution, same failure modes, same confident wrong turns. At least one verifier must be from a different model family than the executor.

principle.name: Frozen contract outranks every LLM judgment

design-principles.principle: A subagent that fails a deterministic gate is rejected regardless of how fluent its explanation is. The LLM judge's verdict is one input among several; every change is gated by a deterministic layer the judge cannot override.
Every layer has a hard token/line budget. Exceeding it is an implementation bug, not a tuning opportunity.

principle.name: Do not tell workers they are ranked

design-principles.principle: Selection happens at the orchestration layer, not in the worker's prompt. Competition-awareness prompting for ephemeral single-task agents risks effort misallocation without quality gain, and offers no selection benefit because there is no subsequent episode to shape.

principle.name: Decompose only when the coordination tax is beaten

design-principles.principle: A naive planner-coder-reviewer pipeline costs 3.22× a single strong call and solves no more tasks. Oracle per-task routing solves 94.3% of runs at half the strong call's cost per solved task. The dividend comes from per-task model choice, not from adding coordination layers.

hard-rules.rule: No subagent is dispatched without a frozen contract a deterministic script can evaluate.
If a criterion cannot be expressed as a command returning pass/fail, it is not ready for delegation.
The worker cannot edit the contract, the hidden tests, or the contract hash.
A worker's "completed" status with an unchecked criterion is unverified and never implies acceptance.
The PM never reads worker code to decide acceptance; it reads gate results.
The architect never reads worker transcripts; it reads the ledger.
At least one verifier per chunk must be from a different model family than the executor.
Every convention lives in exactly one instruction layer; duplication is a defect.
No subagent receives a competitive ranking, leaderboard, or "you are being scored" framing.
The frozen test suite decides when a session is done — not the agent.
Volatile data (timestamps, per-user state) never enters the cached system-prompt prefix.
If the PM encounters a case the contract does not cover, it stops and logs a Spec Gap; it does not guess.

architecture.flow-topology:
Human → Architect → PM → Worker Swarm → Verification Ladder → PM → Architect → Human
The chain is NOT capped at three levels. Intermediate management and verification roles are added when, and only when, they own a failure class no upstream layer can catch.

role.responsibility: Freeze spec, interface contracts, acceptance criteria, out-of-scope, evidence shapes.
Assign verification profile per chunk from risk.
Review evidence ledger and architectural conformance against the frozen spec.
role.does-not-read: Worker code; worker transcripts; PM narratives

role.responsibility: Decompose frozen spec into a dependency graph of atomic chunks.
Classify each chunk into a named role; assign model tier and verification profile.
Dispatch, collect ResultContracts, run gates, compile ledger.
role.constraint: Does not reinterpret the spec. Does not guess Spec Gaps.

role.responsibility: Read-only reconnaissance; reproduce failures; hand off structured evidence.
Implement a bounded chunk in an isolated git worktree.
role.constraint: Sees only the visible smoke test. The hidden suite is the selector.

role.responsibility: Cross-family atomic yes/no checks against the frozen criteria.
role.constraint: Cannot override a deterministic gate failure.
Never emits a scalar score; programmatic code aggregates verdicts.

role.responsibility: Generate independent test scenarios from acceptance criteria; test the artifact as a black box.
role.constraint: Does not see the worker's test plan.
role.catches: Silent mocking, integration drift, spec-gap resolutions, post-hoc confirmation tests.

role.responsibility: Check interface conformance and seam behavior between modules from different workers.
role.activation: Only when interface drift is a named failure class for the project.

context-firewall.rule: The architect and PM operate on compiled evidence, never raw worker transcripts.
Workers write artifacts to isolated git worktrees.
The PM receives a ResultContract (schema in return-contracts).
Verbose tool output is filtered by 80–98% before reaching the orchestrator.
Inter-agent transfers are structured (JSON schema-validated), never free-form prose.
context-firewall.evidence: Free-text handoffs are the main source of context loss; malformed structure becomes a hallucination relay.

required-fields.field: Binary pass/fail, expressed as rerunnable commands or git checks. Example: `pytest tests/hidden/test_rate_limit.py::test_429_on_burst` exits 0
Public interfaces the artifact must expose.
Proof format per criterion: exit code, log line, file existence, hash.
Visible smoke test for the worker; hidden suite hashed and stored outside the worker's write scope. Hidden suite determines selection.
The ResultContract fields the worker must populate.

freezing-rules.rule: Contract is SHA-256 hashed and stored outside the worker's write scope before dispatch.
Worker cannot edit criteria, hidden tests, or the contract hash.
Completion is derived from recorded evidence, not from the worker's completion claim.
The orchestrator re-verifies the worker's return before accepting it.

frozen-acceptance-contract.spec-gap-protocol: When the PM encounters a case the contract does not cover: 1. Stop. 2. Log a Spec Gap with the exact uncovered case. 3. Escalate to the architect. The PM must not guess. Guessing propagates specification failures downstream.

verification-ladder.design-rule: Verification is defense in depth, ordered by marginal cost. Each layer is justified by the failure class it uniquely catches, not by its overall catch rate. Layers must be independent — correlated failures defeat the model.

layer.name: Deterministic pre-gates
layer.catches: Compilation, lint, typecheck, schema validation, file existence, exit codes.
layer.rule: Classes that are decidable belong in a script, never in an agent prompt.
Deterministic acceptance checks outrank every LLM judgment.
A subagent failing L0 is rejected regardless of explanation fluency.

layer.name: Worker self-check
layer.catches: Obvious failures; reduces wasted reviewer cycles.
layer.rule: Never the acceptance authority. Workers are structurally optimistic.

layer.name: Cross-family peer verifier
layer.catches: Correlated blind spots of the executor's model family.
layer.rule: Verifier must be from a different model family than the executor.
Atomic yes/no per criterion; code aggregates the answers. No scalar scores.
layer.evidence: Same-family maker/checker split is two passes with one set of blind spots.

layer.name: Independent QA / holdout
layer.catches: Silent mocking, integration drift, spec-gap resolutions, confirmation tests written to pass.
layer.rule: QA generates its own scenarios from acceptance criteria, without seeing the worker's test plan.
Tests the artifact as a black box.

layer.name: Integration verifier
layer.catches: Cross-module interface drift and seam failures no single-module verifier owns.
layer.rule: Activate only when interface drift is a named failure class for the project.
Adding an integration verifier when modules are independent is pure overhead.

layer.name: Architect acceptance
layer.catches: Architectural conformance; residual Spec Gaps; split verdicts needing escalation.
layer.rule: Reserved for residuals only architectural knowledge can adjudicate.

profile.name: light
profile.when: Trivial, reversible, covered by existing tests

profile.name: standard
profile.when: Ordinary feature work, bounded blast radius

model-routing-policy.efficiency-metric: cost_per_passing_build = (sum of all attempt costs for a task class) / (number of tasks where at least one attempt passed the hidden suite) Tokens per attempt is the wrong metric. It ignores retries, failures, and escalations.
model-routing-policy.capability-profiler: For every model × task class pair, maintain: hidden-suite pass rate p (per single attempt) cost per passing build (including retries and escalations) integration pass rate (on tasks that must integrate with a fixed reference module) reliability@k estimate from ≥5 independent rollouts Profiler is updated after every dispatch. It replaces global benchmark reputation.

routing-rule.step: 1. Classify the chunk into a named agent role.
2. Look up the task-class profile for that role.
3. Select the cheapest model whose cost-per-passing-build clears the chunk threshold AND whose reliability@k clears the risk threshold.
4. If no model clears the threshold, escalate one tier.
5. If the frontier tier fails, either decompose the chunk further or return it to the architect as a Spec Gap.

parallel-redundancy.rule: When a cheap model's single-attempt pass rate is p, run N independent builders in isolated worktrees.
Probability of at least one passing = 1 - (1-p)^N (pass@N).
Choose N to clear the acquisition target subject to a cost ceiling; compare parallel cost against escalating a rung.
Winner is selected by the frozen hidden suite, never by builder self-reports.

model-tier-mapping.tier: Bounded mechanical work, read-only reconnaissance, search, grep, formatting.
Ordinary implementation, editing, testing, standard review.
Architecture, security, hard diagnosis, adversarial review, final adjudication.

metric-distinction.pass-at-k: At least one of k attempts succeeds. Optimistic. Use for acquisition.
metric-distinction.pass-hat-k: All k attempts succeed. Use for customer-facing reliability and delegation scope.
metric-distinction.sampling-rule: At least 5 independent rollouts are necessary to estimate reliability meaningfully.
metric-distinction.warning: Single-rollout proxy correlates with reliability@5 at only Spearman ρ=0.42 — below the 0.70 usefulness threshold.

scope-bounding-rule.formula: P_joint = ∏(i=1..M) p_i where p_i is the model's pass rate on subcomponent i
scope-bounding-rule.action-if-below-threshold: Either (a) reduce M (fewer interfaces), (b) escalate the riskiest subcomponents to a more reliable model, or (c) retain architect review of integration seams.
scope-bounding-rule.example: Builder with 0.85 hidden-suite pass rate × 6 independent subcomponents → 0.85^6 ≈ 0.38 joint reliability. Do not delegate six independent modules to that model without redundancy or escalation.

reliability-and-scope.integration-risk-rule: Delegation budget is set by integration risk, not by module count. Per-module pass rate is not the same as pass rate when modules interact. integration pass rate on a small set of tasks where the module integrates with a fixed reference module.

instruction-layers.core-rule: Each convention lives in exactly one layer; the others point to it or stay silent. Precedence on conflict: L4 (user message) > L3 (task prompt) > L2 (.agentrules) > L1 (system prompt). Specificity wins. But the design rule is to avoid conflicts by construction.

layer.name: System prompt
layer.authority: Identity, safety, tool definitions, output schema, refusal boundaries.

composition.section: All-model behavioral rules, tool use, output format, safety.
Targeted corrections for this model family.
Narrow, auditable adjustments for this model ID.

overlay-rules.rule: Additive layers over a shared core — never branching prompt trees.
Family and exact-model rules must be evidence-driven and narrower than the shared core.
Per-model guidance keyed by model ID in one place; never spread across packages.
Only add an overlay when a model has a documented, authoritative quirk with a vendor-guide citation.
Routing is by model family, not by provider or runtime.

caching-discipline.rule: System prompt is the most expensive layer per token because it is always present.
Prompt caching can reduce input cost by up to 90% — only if the cached prefix stays byte-stable.
Volatile data (timestamps, per-user context, live state) goes in the volatile tail, never the cached prefix.
Monitor stable-prefix ratio and section hashes to detect cache-breaking changes.

layer.name: .agentrules / AGENTS.md
layer.authority: Project-specific rules that apply to every task in that scope.

discovery.precedence: global < workspace < directory. More specific directory rules take priority. Rules are cumulative, not replacement-based.

activation-modes.mode: Full content injected on every call. Use when the rule must hold for every task in scope.
Only path and description pre-injected; agent reads full rule on demand. Use for detailed domain guidance.
Activated when the agent interacts with matching files. Use for path-scoped conventions.
Explicit invocation only. Use for rare or dangerous procedures.

content-rules.rule: Positive specification over negative patching. Replace DO NOT blocks with a single positive specification. Negative instructions can prime the forbidden behavior and bloat the prompt.
Commands section: exact, runnable, one-shot non-interactive forms. A command that never exits hangs an agent.
Three-tier boundaries: Always (run the gate command), Ask first (new dependency, schema migration), Never (edit generated files, commit secrets). Each Never line carries a one-clause reason.
No hedging words. "Usually," "generally," "try to" are not rules. A rule with exceptions names them; a soft convention is a split, not a rule.
Point, don't paste. "Follow <path/to/exemplar>" survives refactors; a pasted template drifts within weeks.
Use pipe-delimited indexes for file trees. Cuts tokens by 70–80% while remaining parseable by major models.
Root .agentrules is a bridge, not a dump. It links to the canonical AGENTS.md and contains only quick-reference essentials.

length-budget.rule: Active rule content should stay under 150 lines. Beyond ~150 lines, extra rules often hurt accuracy.
Path-scoped rule files: 10–30 lines per rule file.

layer.name: Task prompt / skill content
layer.authority: What is true for this phase or task class.

required-structure.field: One sentence: what this agent is responsible for, and what it is not.
Path to the scoped rule file the agent must follow.
The ResultContract fields the agent must populate.
When to stop and return rather than continue.
The recommended input format for this model class (see format-policy).

length-budget.rule: Task prompt: ≤ 500 tokens. Structured, no prose padding.

layer.name: Model specification
layer.authority: Model choice and input format are part of the instruction configuration, not an afterthought.

pinned-per-role.attribute: frontier / mid / fast, tied to role responsibility.
For auditability and prompt overlay keying.

layer.name: Harness enforcement
layer.rationale: Instructions in the context window are subject to attention degradation. Hooks and validators live in the infrastructure and fire regardless of attention state. The prompt teaches judgment and declares invariants; hooks and validators enforce them.

mechanisms.mechanism: Syntax checks, file-shape checks, CLI policy, gate commands.
Rejects malformed ResultContract before content is read.

tier.name: Apex kernel
tier.content: Project description (one line), build commands, critical invariants, phase router.
tier.budget: Under 150 lines total; active rule content under 5–10% of the context window.
tier.purpose: Tells the agent where to go, not the deep details of how to execute.

tier.name: Phase directors / path-scoped rules
tier.content: Local orchestrator instructions, which skills to use, exit criteria for the phase.
tier.activation: trigger: glob (file pattern) OR trigger: model_decision (inject path and description only; agent reads full rule on demand).
tier.rule: On phase transition, drop the prior phase director from active context.

tier.name: Execution skills
tier.content: Deep operational protocols, anti-rationalization tables, evidence requirements.
tier.rule: Once a skill is completed, drop it from active context.
Skill files contain only phase definitions and pointers — not embedded references — to avoid recursive loading.

read-and-drop-discipline.rule: Do not read the entire skills/ directory at once.
When routed to a phase, read ONLY that phase's director file.
When the director says to execute a specific skill, read ONLY that specific file.
Active context after loading must be: apex kernel + current phase director + active skill. Nothing else.

instruction-neglect-prevention.warning: If an agent loads all skill files simultaneously, the noise ratio becomes too high and it reverts to baseline training behaviors, ignoring the strict protocols.
instruction-neglect-prevention.rule: Monitor compliance ceiling; prune before adding.

budget.enforcement: linter warning; loader truncates with alert

context-firewall.rule: Orchestrator and architect never receive raw subagent transcripts.
Verbose tool output filtered by 80–98% before reaching the orchestrator.
Subagents run in isolated context windows with only the brief and inputs they need.
Subagent context is discarded on return.

handoff-size-rule.rule: Handoff artifacts should target ~500 tokens. If a handoff exceeds 500 tokens, it includes details the next agent can discover by reading the code.
Structured handoffs (JSON schema-validated) yield 30–60% higher accuracy than free-form prose.

format-tax.finding: Structured output requirements (JSON, XML, LaTeX, Markdown) substantially degrade reasoning and writing performance across open-weight models. The dominant cost enters at the prompt: format-requesting instructions alone cause most of the accuracy loss, before any decoder constraint is applied.
Few-shot examples and schema descriptions leave most of the degradation intact.
What works: decoupling reasoning from formatting — generate freeform first, then reformat in a second pass; or enable extended thinking within a single generation.
Most recent closed-weight models show little to no format tax.

format-selection-matrix.row: Rationale: structured output taxes open-weight reasoning.

row.format: json or markdown with consistent schema

format-selection-matrix.row: Rationale: consistent formatting improves efficiency and stability.

row.format: markdown or json matching vendor conventions

format-selection-matrix.row: Rationale: little to no format tax; vendor alignment helps.
Rationale: mechanical aggregation; no reasoning about format.

format-policy.measurement-rule: Format choice must be measured, not assumed. Track cost-per-passing-build and hidden-suite pass rate by format for each model × task class pair. Select the format that minimizes cost without degrading quality.

result-contract.rule: Every worker returns this structure. A "completed" status with an unchecked criterion is unverified and never implies acceptance.
The subagent never returns prose. If the schema is invalid, the return is rejected before any content is read.
Skipped verification steps must be recorded as SKIPPED:<reason> from a closed vocabulary; PASS cannot be claimed for a skipped check.

architect-ledger.rule: The architect returns a pass/fail ledger to the human, not a narrative.
architect-ledger.columns: criterion | disposition | evidence digest | verification layers passed
architect-ledger.human-review: Human samples the ledger and verifies high-risk entries against artifacts. Human does not re-read the code.

agent-definition-schema.description: Binds all four specification axes: .agentrules scope, system-prompt composition, task-prompt template, and model (family, exact ID, format).
agent-definition-schema.schema:
agent: id: "coder-python" role: "executor"
model: family: "anthropic" exact_id: "claude-sonnet-4" tier: "mid" input_format: "markdown" # prose | markdown | json | binary_schema
system_prompt: base: "prompts/harness_core.md" family_overlay: "prompts/overlays/anthropic.md" exact_delta: "prompts/deltas/claude-sonnet-4.md" cache_stable: true
agentrules: global: "~/.gemini/AGENTS.md" project: "AGENTS.md" path_scoped: - glob: "**/*.py" rule: ".agents/rules/python.md" trigger: "glob" - description: "Database migration conventions" rule: ".agents/rules/migrations.md" trigger: "model_decision"
task_prompt: template: "prompts/tasks/implement_module.md" max_tokens: 500 acceptance_contract: "contracts/{{task_id}}.yml" return_schema: "schemas/ResultContract.json"
verification: profile: "standard" # light | standard | heavy cross_family_verifier: true
context: max_active_rules_lines: 150 drop_completed_skills: true context_firewall: true

architect-decision-procedure.description: For each chunk in the decomposition graph:
architect-decision-procedure.step: CLASSIFY the chunk into a named role (scout, plan-verifier, mech-executor, executor, verifier, security-reviewer, security-executor). If no role fits → decompose further.
ASSIGN verification profile from risk: Light (trivial) · Standard (ordinary) · Heavy (security / migration / irreversible).
ASSIGN model tier from the task-class profile: cheapest tier whose cost-per-passing-build clears the chunk threshold. If none clears → escalate one rung.
FREEZE the acceptance contract on disk: rerunnable commands, evidence shapes, out-of-scope, return schema. Hash it. Store outside the worker's write scope.
DISPATCH with a brief containing: role boundary, frozen contract path, return schema, stop conditions, format hint. No competitive framing. No leaderboard.

ON RETURN, run the gate: L0 deterministic gates first (sole authority for mechanical failure). L2 cross-family verifier only if L0 passes. L3 independent QA for standard/heavy profiles. L4 integration verifier only for multi-module projects. Reject any "completed" claim contradicting a failed gate.
COMPILE the verdict into the architect's ledger: criterion → disposition → evidence digest. Do not include the subagent's narrative in the ledger.
UPDATE the task-class profile: cost per passing build, hidden-suite pass rate, verifier accuracy.

stopping-rule.rule: The frozen test suite decides when a session is done — not the agent.
Once every acceptance criterion in the frozen contract has a disposition of pass (or a documented, escalated Spec Gap), the cycle terminates.
The architect does not continue generating work after the contract is satisfied.
stopping-rule.evidence: Hierarchical systems frequently continue past acceptance: two-thirds of rounds can occur after implementation was accepted.

phase.name: Contract and rule-store foundation

deliverables.item: Frozen acceptance contract template with required fields.
Hash-and-freeze mechanism; worker write-scope isolation.
Layer 0 deterministic gate runner (compilation, lint, typecheck, schema validation, test runner).
ResultContract JSON schema and validator.
Scoped .agentrules / AGENTS.md discovery with directory-tree walk and precedence resolution.
YAML frontmatter parser for always_on / model_decision / glob / manual.
Rule linter: positive-specification check, hedging-word detection, line-budget enforcement.

phase.gate: A trivial task can be dispatched against a frozen contract; the worker cannot modify the contract or hidden tests. An agent editing a subdirectory file receives the correct cumulative rule set.

phase.name: Verification ladder and progressive disclosure

deliverables.item: Layer 2 cross-family peer verifier with atomic binary schema and programmatic aggregation.
Layer 3 independent QA holdout test generator.
PM decomposition engine: dependency graph, atomic chunking, role classification, verification-profile assignment.
Context firewall: PM receives ResultContract, not transcripts.
Three-tier progressive disclosure loader; read-and-drop mechanism; per-layer budget enforcement.

phase.gate: A multi-chunk task dispatches, verifies through L0–L3, and compiles into a ledger without the PM reading worker code. A multi-phase agent never holds more than apex kernel + current phase director + active skill.

phase.name: Capability profiler, routing, and prompt caching

deliverables.item: Task-class capability profiler populated from ≥5 rollouts per model per task class.
Cost-per-passing-build and reliability@k calculator.
Routing policy: cheapest model clearing threshold, escalate on failure.
Parallel redundancy dispatch with hidden-suite selection.
Stable-prefix system-prompt composer; volatile tail; cache-hit monitoring.

phase.gate: Routing decisions improve cost per passing build on a held-out task class without reducing hidden-suite pass rate. Repeated calls achieve ≥80% cache hit rate on the system-prompt prefix.

phase.name: Integration verifier and heavy-profile hardening

deliverables.item: Layer 4 integration verifier for multi-module seams.
Heavy-profile workflow: Layers 0–5 plus human approval for security/migration tasks.
Scope-bounding calculator integrated into PM dispatch.
Architect final ledger review workflow.
Model-family overlays and exact-model deltas with vendor-guide citations.

phase.gate: A multi-module project with a security-sensitive component completes through the Heavy profile; the human can sample-verify the ledger in under 15 minutes. Routing to a different model family uses the correct overlay and format without manual reconfiguration.

phase.name: Format policy and context isolation

deliverables.item: Format-selection matrix integrated into agent definitions.
.agentrules progressive-disclosure template per task class.
Format A/B measurement: cost per passing build and hidden-suite pass rate by format.
Subagent isolation: fresh context window containing only brief and inputs.
Context firewall: 80–98% filtering of verbose tool output.
Structured inter-agent protocol: JSON schema-validated contracts between router and specialists.

phase.gate: PM selects the input format minimizing cost per passing build per model × task class. Orchestrator context stays below budget while a subagent processes a tool-output-heavy task.

evaluation-metrics.metric: Total attempt cost ÷ tasks with ≥1 hidden-suite pass.
Fraction of tasks clearing the frozen hidden suite.
Fraction of k independent rollouts where all pass.
Minutes on ledger sampling vs. code reading.
Fraction of tasks hitting an unresolved spec ambiguity.
Fraction of accepted builds that later fail real-world use.
Total lines of .agentrules in context. Target: ≤ 150.
Fraction of calls reusing the cached prefix. Target: ≥ 80%.
Fraction of rules followed on spot-check tasks.
Tasks where a late-session rule violation occurs.
evaluation-metrics.non-metric: Does not optimize for raw pass@k. It inflates under repeated sampling and overstates customer-facing reliability.

risk.name: Coordination tax exceeds heterogeneity dividend
risk.mitigation: Gate every decomposition behind the break-even rule: decompose only when the expected saving from cheaper roles exceeds handoff cost.

risk.name: Worker self-tests are optimistic
risk.mitigation: Hidden suite is the sole selector. L3 QA generates independent tests from the contract, not from the worker's tests.

risk.name: Same-family review shares blind spots
risk.mitigation: L2 peer verifier must be a different model family than the executor.

risk.name: Over-decomposition
risk.mitigation: Add an intermediate layer only when it owns a failure class no upstream layer can catch. Measure coordination-overhead ratio.

risk.name: Format tax degrades open-weight reasoning
risk.mitigation: Decouple reasoning from formatting for reasoning-heavy steps. Measure format choice by cost-per-passing-build, not parse success.

risk.name: Context drift in long projects
risk.mitigation: Context firewall. PM receives ResultContract; architect receives ledger. No raw transcripts in judgment contexts.

risk.name: Post-completion loops
risk.mitigation: Frozen test suite defines done; architect terminates on all-pass ledger.

risk.name: Drift bombs from duplicated rules
risk.mitigation: One rule, one layer; other layers point or stay silent.

risk.name: Cache-breaking system-prompt changes
risk.mitigation: Byte-stable prefix; volatile data in the tail; stable-prefix monitoring.

risk.name: Model-family mismatch
risk.mitigation: Additive overlays over shared core; narrow exact-model deltas; vendor-guide evidence.

risk.name: Subagent inherits nothing
risk.mitigation: Explicit injection protocol; critical constraints passed at invocation.

risk.name: Reward hacking by competition-aware agents
risk.mitigation: Do not tell workers they are ranked. Selection happens at the orchestration layer. Hidden checks the worker cannot edit.

risk.name: Spec-gap guessing
risk.mitigation: PM stops and logs Spec Gaps; does not guess. Architect resolves or decomposes further.

definition-of-done.criterion: Every agent definition specifies .agentrules scope, system-prompt composition, task-prompt template, and model (family, exact ID, format).
Rule discovery resolves cumulative scopes with correct precedence and zero duplicated rules across layers.
Progressive disclosure ensures no agent loads more than the apex kernel plus its current phase director and active skill.
System-prompt prefixes are byte-stable and achieve ≥80% cache hit rate on repeated calls.
Model-family overlays and exact-model deltas are keyed by model ID and documented with vendor-guide evidence.
The context firewall keeps the orchestrator's active context below budget while subagents process tool-heavy work.
The verification ladder catches a seeded failure at the layer designed to catch it (qualification test for each layer).
The capability profiler recalibrates routing from at least 20 observed task executions.
The PM can dispatch a multi-chunk task, route each chunk by task-class profile, and compile a ledger without reading worker code.
The human can verify a completed project by sampling the architect's ledger — not by reading every prompt or every line of code.

project-specification.closing-principle: The architect's competence is not in reading the builder's code. It is in freezing the contract, owning the verification ladder, and routing each verification layer to the cheapest agent and format that can clear it reliably. The best way to free up a model's working context is not to write less, but to load less — and to move every decidable rule out of the prompt and into the harness. Instructions teach judgment; hooks enforce invariants; progressive disclosure loads only what the current step requires; and model-specific overlays ensure the same instruction is expressed in the format each model was trained to follow.
